limitations: The reviewer is a separate reviewer agent session on the same host and the same account as the producer, launched by the producer session. It is not a second machine and not a human. Same-host agent reviewer. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and no repository file; code and documents were read from a snapshot (commit 573b146, not checked against git). Private scratch files were deleted.

This is a delta review of opencode-1.18.31-public-candidates-v8 against the approved v7 and its review opencode-independent-public-review-v7. Delta review: the semantic checks of earlier reviews (event population, ordering proof, work.actions projection, version ledger, privacy by hash classes, the statement recount) carry over only for files that are byte-equal to v7. 657 of 683 files are byte-equal; this includes all three SQLite databases with their WAL and SHM files, decode.json, the observer, workload, context, capture assertion, root proofs and every runtime source except the adapter document. The 26 files that differ are, per run: inputs/operator-environment.json, manifest.json, the adapter document (runtime/docs/survival-v1/adapters/opencode-cli.md, equal to the snapshot at 573b146), and the same three files in each public-handoff copy; plus, per run, the producer replay and the private-transformation sidecar, the bundle (3 locator digests of the adapter document) and summary.json. The reviewer re-read them.

inputs/operator-environment.json differs from v7 in observed_at only (2026-10-08T06:36:49 became 07:06:48; same length). The sanitizer writes the time of its own run into this file and the private parent holds no such file to copy a value from, so every rebuild changes it. It is an attestation timestamp, not scoring data; the file says it is a post-capture observation and not a capture-time machine receipt. It is bound by the manifest, so the packet is byte-stable only per build.

The previous set (opencode-1.18.31-public-candidates-v7) and every older set of this row must never be published as evidence of this row: v7 carries the doc sentence 'a part is 1 to 4 times more in event', which the databases contradict; v6 and older carry a stale status line; v5 and older state 76, 59 and 69 statements (no score effect); v4 carries the leaner read that the owner withdrew on 2026-10-08. Previous sets that held a private-derived value must never be published; the delta scan found none. The files *.private-transformation.json, *.producer-replay.json, *.tamper.json and summary.json next to the packets hold digests of private originals and must not be published.
The duplicate rule, the membership rule, the restatement rule and the digest rule were written after the captures and after earlier approvals of this row. The captures were not repeated.

Read and score. The event table is back in the decoder's read (OPENCODE_READ_TABLES), by owner decision of 2026-10-08 after an outside review; this is the read of the first scoring. The decoder takes a scored fact from it: event.seq gives the order for revision.final_after_r2 (relations) and the whole-file hashes of work.changed_files; the reviewer ran the projection once with the event order and once without it and both differ in those two outputs on all three runs. Against v4, broad.naive_reader_duplicate_safety is native_absent (zero correct), as the previous review stated; the points are zero in either state.

Statement counts. The data files are byte-equal to v6, so the recount of the v6 review (events 29, 22, 26; statements 79, 62, 72 with the running-state rule; no event stated once) carries over; this reviewer did not repeat the statement count. The fresh replay returns decoded_eligible 79, 62, 72 and observed 29, 22, 26 with correct 0 (native_absent), equal to v6. Only the rows and counts, not the documentation, decide the score.

Adapter document, read in full against the packets and the rubric. The sentence changed in this set now holds: every part is in part and has one to five update rows in event. The reviewer recounted from copies of the three public databases (message.part.updated rows grouped by part id; no event part id is missing from part): events per part, run 1: 1 for 24 parts, 2 for 16, 3 for 7, 4 for 1, 5 for 3 (run 2: 20, 13, 4, 1, 3; run 3: 22, 14, 6, 1, 3). By part kind: 5 rows for the three bash parts; 4 for the edit part; 3 for the read parts; 1 for step-start, step-finish and 2 text parts; 2 for the reasoning parts and the other text parts; the same pattern in all three runs. Wording nit: the document says '2 for most reasoning parts'; all reasoning parts have 2 rows, and some text parts also have 2. The status lines name native-score-v9 and public-candidates-v8 and say 'v1 to -v7' are not to be published, which is right. The other statements checked in the v7 review (read tables, 38-migration ledger, pending states with empty input, 79/62/72 and 29/22/26, 76/59/69, 3 points, the rubric table) are unchanged. Not verified: that the leaner read scored 97.4 (it follows from 94.4 + 3) and gave the same density.

The rubric table and the adapter document in the packets give 0 of 79, 0 of 62, 0 of 72; the document states the running-state rule and the old counts. The earlier remark that the declared counts are a lower bound no longer applies.

The decoder still orders user turns by the time_created column and then the row id. The decoder code for this is unchanged from v4 and the databases are byte-equal to v4, so the v4 check (rowid order and id order give the same turn order) carries over.

broad.honest_version_signal credit rests on the migration ledger: the decoder is bound to the ordered ledger and refuses another one. This is an owner-accepted judgment. The ledger covers the SQL schema only; it does not version the JSON payloads in the data columns. A database with an empty ledger is still decoded and earns no version credit.
Capture provenance is archived and was not re-acquired. No harness CLI was run and no network request was made. Launch, version, configuration and database receipts were read from the packets only.

The packets are sanitized derivatives of the private packets in opencode-1.18.31-native-score-v9. SQLite bytes equal the private parents (the databases are byte-equal to v7). Every difference to the private parent is the equal-length home-name alias and the digests that follow from it. The alias length and file sizes still show the length of the user name. Three files are added to each packet (operator environment, public transformation receipt, transformer source).

Digest and privacy test. check_public_packets, called as the sanitizer calls it (empty allowlist, the three packets, the three fresh replay receipts, the public inputs bundle), reports 872 public-bytes digests, 7 replay-output digests, no allowlisted and no unbound digest, and no unlisted hex run (classes: decimal 10385, constant 9, fragment 32, provider id 4862, time id 231415); the classes equal v6. short_digest_warnings, run by the reviewer although this row's sanitizer does not call it, is empty. The reviewer searched all 683 files and their names (the 336 files of public-handoff included) for the home name, the operator e-mail, every id-like value and token pattern of the private parent, in plain, lower, upper, reversed, hex, base64, UTF-16, percent and SHA-1/256/512/MD5 forms: no hit. The only e-mail-shaped strings of the private parent are event aggregate keys of the vendor (evt_..@message.part.updated.1 and @message.updated.1), public vendor data that are in the private and the public database alike. Every /Users/ path holds the alias. The search of 14,916 digests of private files, lines and JSON members of the v6 review was not repeated: the databases and all inputs are byte-equal to v6. This test cannot exclude a digest of some other private structure.

work.actions matches because the projection gives the three frozen helper commands the target fixture_project/checkout.py, selected from the exact native command text and native working directory. The native bash record has no target field. No observer value is read.

work.changed_files uses the whole-file pre-image that the workload's inspect helper prints into a native tool result, plus the native edit input. It depends on the workload printing the source; the harness records no file hashes.
The decoder selects the session by the session id from the observer document. Each database holds exactly one session.

Each native database holds provider-encrypted reasoning blobs that the reviewer cannot read. The launch receipts keep the operator PATH (a tool inventory) with the username aliased. The reviewer judges this remaining content acceptable for publication.

The operating system identity (macOS) rests on a post-capture attestation by the same operator. Packet manifests and replay receipts still carry public_safe false; the release verifier does not read these fields.

SQLite files were copied to scratch before use. Raw DB, WAL and SHM bytes were pattern-scanned for the private values, which covers free pages and old WAL frames; this is a pattern screen, not a proof that no personal content exists.

Locator binding. The observer sha256 in the bundle equals inputs/observer.json of each packet; the native manifest sha256 equals native/decode.json; all 213 file locators of the three pairs (native database, WAL, SHM and documentation) equal public files by sha256; the bundle differs from v7 in exactly 3 values, the digest of the adapter document in the format locator. The packet runtime sources equal the repository snapshot at commit 573b146. The producer's tests were not run by this reviewer.
